item.title: Hip Long-Axis / Lateral Traction
patientPosition: Supine, hip in comfortable resting position.
For lateral traction, hip may be slightly flexed/abducted according to technique.
therapistPosition: At foot end for long-axis traction or beside hip for belt-assisted lateral traction.
stabilization: Pelvis stabilized manually or with belt.
contact: Long-axis: secure distal leg above ankle without compressing sensitive structures.
Lateral: belt/contact around proximal femur as trained.
forceDirection: Lateral traction pulls femoral head laterally from acetabulum.
dosage: 10–30 second holds × 3–5 repetitions or sustained longer bouts if tolerated.
safety: Avoid fracture, dislocation, severe osteoporosis or acute postoperative restrictions.
item.visualCue: Pelvis fixed → Femur distracted along shaft/laterally → Re-test hip motion.

subTechniques.name: Hip Lateral Traction
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Reduce joint compression and improve flexion/rotation tolerance in selected stiff/painful hips.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the hip flexed slightly into a comfortable resting position.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the pelvis. Use a belt or broad proximal-thigh contact to control the femur close to the joint.
subTechniques.direction: Distract the femoral head laterally, perpendicular to the acetabular treatment plane.
subTechniques.reassess: Hip flexion/internal rotation, squat and walking.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: A belt can reduce therapist effort but does not replace precise pelvic stabilization.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Respect hip replacement precautions and fracture risk.

subTechniques.name: Posterior Hip Translatoric Glide
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the hip flexed to the treatment position and pelvis stabilized.
subTechniques.contact: Broad contact through the proximal femur/knee line while preventing pelvic rotation.
subTechniques.direction: Apply a sustained posterior glide parallel to the treatment plane after taking up slack.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: If the pelvis rotates backward, the movement is no longer isolated at the hip.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid in acute hip injury or unstable postoperative state.
